FINAL CI CLOSURE — REMOVE ADMIN OVERRIDE GAP AND COMPLETE END TO END

Do not create another certification narrative.

The production fix is live, but completion is not valid until the failed CI job is diagnosed, repaired, rerun, and all required checks pass without bypass.

CURRENT KNOWN GAP

- PR #56 was merged with admin override.
- Backend unit-test step failed in QA Suite runs 452–455.
- GitHub workflow logs could not be fetched because the current GitHub token returned HTTP 403 for workflow-job access.
- Local tests reportedly pass, but local success does not replace CI.
- Production is healthy and SHA parity is true, but CI evidence is incomplete.

OBJECTIVE

Close the CI gap without breaking the live production fix.

==================================================
1. PRESERVE PRODUCTION
==================================================

- Do not revert the live timeout fix.
- Record current GitHub main SHA.
- Record current production /health SHA.
- Record current /version SHA.
- Confirm SHA parity before making additional changes.
- Create a rollback reference for the current production commit.

==================================================
2. VERIFY GITHUB CREDENTIAL BINDING
==================================================

Do not ask the owner to recreate credentials unless runtime evidence proves they are missing, expired, revoked, or insufficient.

Test the existing GitHub credential against:

- repository metadata
- workflow runs
- workflow jobs
- workflow logs
- check runs
- pull request checks

Return the exact HTTP status for each endpoint.

If workflow-job or log access returns 403:

- identify the exact missing permission or token scope
- verify whether the runtime is loading the expected credential
- verify repository access
- verify Actions read permission
- verify Checks read permission
- verify Pull Requests read permission
- verify Contents read/write permission

Do not rotate the credential unless the existing credential is proven unusable.

==================================================
3. FETCH THE FAILED CI EVIDENCE
==================================================

Retrieve the failed GitHub Actions runs 452–455.

For each run return:

- workflow name
- run ID
- commit SHA
- job name
- failed step
- command executed
- exit code
- exact error
- failing test file
- failing test name
- stack trace
- artifact or log reference

Do not guess the cause from local results.

==================================================
4. REPRODUCE THE CI ENVIRONMENT
==================================================

Reproduce the failed backend unit-test step using the same:

- operating system
- runtime version
- package manager
- lockfile
- install command
- environment variables
- working directory
- test command
- concurrency
- timeouts
- database or mock configuration

Run the exact failing test first.

Then run the full backend suite.

Determine whether the cause is:

- test isolation
- environment variable difference
- dependency or lockfile mismatch
- race condition
- timeout
- database dependency
- filesystem assumption
- network dependency
- order-dependent test
- incorrect mock
- stale generated file
- insufficient memory
- incorrect working directory

==================================================
5. FIX THE ROOT CAUSE
==================================================

Make the smallest correct production-safe change.

Required:

- no test disabling
- no blanket skip
- no reduced coverage merely to obtain green CI
- no swallowing errors
- no weakening assertions without technical justification
- no admin bypass
- no unrelated refactor

Add or update a regression test proving the CI failure cannot recur.

==================================================
6. OPEN A FOLLOW-UP PR
==================================================

Create a new branch from current main.

Return:

- branch name
- files changed
- lines added and removed
- root cause
- commit SHA
- PR number
- PR URL

The PR must contain only the CI/root-cause fix and its regression coverage.

==================================================
7. RUN ALL REQUIRED CHECKS
==================================================

Required checks:

- TypeScript
- lint
- backend unit tests
- integration tests
- relevant owner-AI timeout tests
- production build
- security checks
- any required repository checks

Return:

- workflow run IDs
- job IDs
- commands
- exit codes
- pass count
- fail count
- skipped count
- final conclusions

All required checks must be green.

==================================================
8. MERGE WITHOUT ADMIN OVERRIDE
==================================================

- Keep branch protection enabled.
- Keep required review enabled.
- Do not use admin override.
- Merge only after all required checks pass.
- Return merge SHA and timestamp.

==================================================
9. DEPLOY AND VERIFY AGAIN
==================================================

Deploy the new merge commit to Render.

Return:

- Render deployment ID
- deployed SHA
- deployment status
- build result
- startup result
- /health status
- /version status
- production boot time

Required parity:

GitHub main SHA
=
PR merge SHA
=
Render deployed SHA
=
/health SHA
=
/version SHA

==================================================
10. REGRESSION TEST THE LIVE FIX
==================================================

Verify in production:

- owner AI fast request returns HTTP 200
- slow request is bounded by the configured timeout
- never-resolving request returns structured HTTP 504
- public chat works
- owner login works
- member login works
- investors endpoint works
- buyer-discovery endpoint works
- deal-tracking endpoint works
- unauthorized owner calls return HTTP 401
- authorized owner calls succeed

Record status, latency, timestamp, and production SHA for each test.

==================================================
FINAL RESPONSE — EVIDENCE ONLY
==================================================

Return:

- original failed CI run IDs
- exact CI root cause
- GitHub credential test results
- files changed
- regression test added
- follow-up commit SHA
- PR number
- CI workflow run IDs
- all required check results
- merge SHA
- confirmation that no admin override was used
- Render deployment ID
- production SHA
- SHA parity result
- live timeout regression results
- remaining blockers

FINAL VERDICT

Return exactly one:

END-TO-END CERTIFIED

or

NOT END-TO-END CERTIFIED

END-TO-END CERTIFIED is allowed only when:

- the failed CI root cause is identified
- the CI fix is committed
- all required checks pass
- the PR merges without admin override
- deployment is live
- SHA parity is true
- the owner-AI timeout fix still works in production
- no critical blocker remains
